state.misconception_label: Thinks alternate angles are always equal

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are arguing about alternate angles. Tom says angles \( p \) and \( q \) are alternate. Katie says angles \( p \) and \( q \) are equal. Who is correct? ![Shows two non parallel lines that are intersected by another line. Angles P and Q are both on the outside of the lines and on opposite sides of the transversal.](). I got Only
Katie because I assumed all the angles in the figure are equal.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: In this case, the angles \( p \) and \( q \) are not alternate angles. They are actually vertically opposite angles. Can you explain why they are not alternate angles and why they are equal instead?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Wait, I'm confused now - I thought alternate angles were on opposite sides of the line? So if p and q are on opposite sides of the transversal, why aren't they alternate angles? And you said they're vertically opposite instead, but aren't those the angles that are across from each other at the same point?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's clarify the difference between alternate angles and vertically opposite angles. Alternate angles are on opposite sides of the transversal and are equal, while vertically opposite angles are across from each other at the intersection point and are also equal. Can you see how the angles \( p \) and \( q \) fit this description?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so vertically opposite angles are at the same intersection point... but I'm still a bit confused because p and q are on opposite sides of the transversal, so wouldn't that make them alternate? Like, how do I know if angles are alternate angles or vertically opposite angles if they're both on opposite sides?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher makes a critical mathematical error by claiming p and q are vertically opposite angles when they are at different intersection points, fails to address the core misconception that alternate angles require parallel lines, and the student remains confused throughout with no improvement in understanding.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher makes confusing and incorrect statements (claiming p and q are vertically opposite when they're at different intersection points) rather than providing clear direct explanations or worked examples characteristic of traditional instruction.
